pages.text: The Miner's tier is determined by the controller block at its center; four tiers exist. The structure and size are identical; the tier only changes performance.$(br2)$(li)Basic: progress rate ×1.0, energy capacity 1M, roughly 200 ticks per cycle at full power$(li)Advanced: rate ×1.5, capacity 5M, approximately 133 ticks per cycle$(li)Super: rate ×2.0, capacity 20M, 100 ticks per cycle$(li)Ultimate: rate ×3.0, capacity 50M, approximately 67 ticks per cycle$(br2)Capacity is the controller's internal power buffer; every tier consumes a base of 10 energy per tick (speed modules add a surcharge).

$(bold)Output:$(reset) all four tiers use the same fixed list of ten vanilla materials: coal, raw iron, raw copper, raw gold, redstone, lapis lazuli, quartz, diamond, emerald and netherite scrap.$(br2)Base weights, high to low: coal 30 / iron 24 / copper 22 / gold 12 / redstone 8 / lapis 6 / quartz 6 / diamond 3 / emerald 2 / scrap 1.$(br2)$(bold)Tier bonus:$(reset) the three rare minerals (diamond, emerald, netherite scrap) have their weight multiplied by ×1.0 / ×1.5 / ×2.0 / ×3.0. A tier never changes the ore list and does not unlock deeper ores or special biomes; it only increases the frequency of rare minerals.

$(bold)Changing tiers:$(reset) break the controller at the center and insert the desired tier; the rest of the miner is unchanged.$(br2)The new controller re-checks the structure, forms again, re-links the ports and resumes operation.$(br2)Note: removing the controller halts the whole miner. Clear the output buffer and the ports first, and confirm the formed state in the interface after the swap.

The Miner Port serves as both the power inlet and the product outlet. In the 9x9x5 layout each miner has one, located at the dead center of the top layer on the same axis as the controller; the bottom center is occupied by the Drill Bit.$(br2)$(bold)Power input:$(reset) the port has a 10M energy buffer for pipes and, once formed, forwards power to the controller without a rate cap.$(br2)$(bold)Product collection:$(reset) the controller pushes ores into the port's 27-slot buffer, and hoppers or item pipes can extract from any slot.$(br2)$(bold)Priority:$(reset) if a Miner Item Output is installed on a pillar, products fill that output first and the port receives only the overflow; items already in the port are transferred to any output with free space (a one-way transfer).$(br2)Additional Miner Energy Input and Miner Item Output blocks can be placed on the pillars; see the Miner Structure entry.
Structure details are in Miner Structure; performance details are in Miner Upgrades; if the grid is insufficient, see the Energy Generator entry first.
